title: 영어브리핑_2026-10-28
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: 원사 미신고 표를 Trinh Do에게 11시까지 받아 점심 전 법인장 보고, Asanka 항공편 선택 확인·Mai 리마인드(랙 재견적 오늘·원장 내일)
paragraphs: Part one. Opening.
Good morning, Anthony. Today is Wednesday, October twenty-eighth. Take a deep breath and enjoy the ride to the factory.

This briefing has eight parts. Part one is your opening. Part two is the top three jobs for today. Part three is the reports you need to collect. Part four is the replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines for the next three days. Part six is English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.
Listen slowly. When you hear a pause, say the sentence out loud. Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. The thread without customs declaration.

Last Saturday, Trinh Do reported that some thread from COATS PHONG PHU came in without a customs declaration. This is thread for Aritzia orders. Yesterday morning you asked her for a table by five p.m. The table should show the invoice number, the date received, the quantity, the amount, and the current stock for each shipment.

As of yesterday afternoon, there was no table in your inbox. Trinh did answer some other items yesterday. She replied about the GOH box work steps, the container size in the remarks column, and the PO numbers in the purchase request description. But two items are still open. The ExIm Ledger for September, with your two questions, was due yesterday. And the thread table did not come.

Why does this matter? The fabric and thread physical count is this Saturday, October thirty-first. The head office will also check the customs balance. If we do not know the numbers before the count, we cannot explain the gap. Mr Moon also needs to decide the next step, such as a late declaration.
Your first action: go to Trinh's desk before nine a.m. Ask for the table by eleven a.m. Then report to Mr Moon with a clear plan before lunch.
Number two. The flight for Mr Asanka, the new sewing manager.

Yesterday you sent Mr Asanka the flight options from Colombo to Da Nang on November fifteenth. One is Malaysia Airlines through Kuala Lumpur. One is SriLankan Airlines through Bangkok. You asked him to choose one and reply by today.

Why does this matter? Ticket prices go up every day. Also, Ms Tho needs the flight date for his E-visa. And there is a gap of about two weeks between Chamin's last day and Mr Asanka's first day. Mr Moon has not yet heard your plan for who will lead sewing during that gap.
Your first action: check Mr Asanka's reply in the morning. Then ask Mai to book the ticket after Mr Moon agrees. In the same talk with Mr Moon, give him your idea for the sewing gap.
Number three. Follow-up with Mai.

Mai has two items. First, the re-quote for the thirty-nine relaxing racks is due today. You asked for the unit price for each item. Second, yesterday you asked her to update the consumables ledger. Her part has not been entered since October thirteenth. That is due tomorrow, Thursday.

Why does this matter? Mai's deadlines need close follow-up, so a short reminder helps. Without the ledger, we cannot check the defect sticker stock. You already told Van to remove the defect stickers from this week's list, because we still have them in stock.
Your first action: at ten a.m., send Mai one short message. Remind her about the rack re-quote today and the ledger tomorrow.
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, Trinh Do. You need three things from her. The thread table. The ExIm Ledger for September with answers to your two questions. And her part of the physical count checklist, which is due tomorrow. Here is a sentence you can use.
Trinh, just a reminder that the thread table and the September ledger were due yesterday. Please send them by eleven a.m. today.

Second, Mint, the fabric warehouse leader. By tomorrow, Mint must finish racks seven and eight. Mint must also give a rack location to the fabric that has no location in the QR system. And the interlining must be kept separate from the fabric. Yesterday Mint said the warehouse still writes the lot number on paper. You replied that the lot number must go into the system, because our goal is to remove paper. Today, check that Mint understands this. Here is a sentence.
Mint, could you confirm whether the lot numbers are now entered in the system, not only on paper?

Third, the broken pallets. Mint reported eight broken pallets in the fabric warehouse. The finishing team reported twenty-three in the finishing warehouse. That is thirty-one in total. You asked for the number and photos before the end of the month. Check that the photos came with the numbers. Here is a sentence.
Thank you for the count. Please send me the photos of the thirty-one damaged pallets by Friday.

Fourth, Ms Tho. Today is the twenty-eighth. Ms Tho checks the EIS organization chart against the real headcount every month on this day. The result goes to the head office for the CEO review on November first. Here is a sentence.
Ms Tho, please update me as soon as the EIS check is done today.

Fifth, Ms Nga in accounting. Yesterday you asked her to update the depreciation list for September. The head office asked for it. Her deadline is tomorrow, Thursday, at five p.m. She already sent a file yesterday afternoon. Check if it has the new September assets, and if the totals match the September books. Here is a sentence.
Ms Nga, I'd like to highlight one point. Please check that the balance matches the September trial balance.
Part four. Replies I owe.

First, Trinh Do asked you a question about the physical count. EXIM has uploaded receipts to the QR system from early October until now. She asked if they also need to upload the history before October. She also gave the customs codes for interlining. Your reply could start like this.
Thank you, Trinh. I will check and tell you by noon whether you need the data before October.
Second, Thùy Dung sent the overtime request for next week, November second to November seventh. It went to Mr Moon and to you for review and approval. Your reply could start like this.
Dear Mr Moon, I have checked next week's overtime request. The hours are within the legal limit, and I have no other comments.
Check the hours first before you write that.

Third, the e-approval system. Trinh Tran sent a new vendor registration for a company called DAI NAM. There is also purchase request DN twenty-six, ten, zero zero four seven, and some older ones from last week. You can review them in the system. If you have a question, your reply could start like this.
Ms Trinh, before I approve, could you tell me why we need a new vendor for this item?
Fourth, Mint and the finishing team on the pallets. A short thank-you is enough. Then ask for the photos, as in part three.
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Wednesday. There is an all-day reminder in your calendar for the monthly stock update for planning. Ms Tho does the EIS check. In the morning, Hecny should return the two repaired makeshift frames for GOH hangers. This is for the Vince shipment. You also have the packing team meeting about the new job types in MANPOWER.

Tomorrow, Thursday, October twenty-ninth. GOH box loading for the Vince shipment. EXIM and the warehouse send their physical count checklist. Ms Nga sends the depreciation list by five p.m. Mai finishes the consumables ledger. There is also an old calendar item called next week overtime report. That task was stopped on October fifteenth, so you can delete it.

Friday, October thirtieth. Mr Kasun from Aritzia visits, with the J Crew pre-production meeting. The local staff information security pledge report is due. The third quarter corporate income tax prepayment is due. And you send the count list to Trinh Tran.
Saturday, October thirty-first. The fabric and thread physical count. It is also Chamin's last day.
Part six. English review.
Let's practice thirteen expressions. Some are from yesterday's card. Some are from Monday. Some are from last Saturday's test, where you missed them.

The expression is, please hold off on. It means, please wait and do not do it yet. For example, please hold off on rejecting the rate until the supplier sends a revised quotation. Now say it with me. Please hold off on booking the ticket until Mr Moon agrees. ... ... ... One more time. Please hold off on booking the ticket until Mr Moon agrees.

The expression is, just a reminder that. You use it to remind someone of a deadline politely. For example, just a reminder that the missing lot numbers are due by Wednesday. Now say it with me. Just a reminder that the rack re-quote is due today. ... ... ... One more time. Just a reminder that the rack re-quote is due today.

The expression is, please update me as soon as. It means, tell me right after something happens. For example, please update me as soon as the flight is booked. Now say it with me. Please update me as soon as Mr Asanka replies. ... ... ... One more time. Please update me as soon as Mr Asanka replies.

The word is, affected. It means, hit by the problem. For example, please let me know the final affected quantity of fabric. Now say it with me. Please tell me the total affected quantity of thread. ... ... ... One more time. Please tell me the total affected quantity of thread.

The word is, address. It means, to deal with a problem or a question. For example, only question number one has been addressed so far. Now say it with me. Two of your questions have not been addressed yet. ... ... ... One more time. Two of your questions have not been addressed yet.

The word is, justify. It means, to give a good reason. For example, please justify the purchase of three units. Now say it with me. Please justify why we need a new vendor. ... ... ... One more time. Please justify why we need a new vendor.

The word is, dedicated. It means, only for one job. For example, please ask the supplier for a dedicated team for GOH box loading. Now say it with me. We need a dedicated team for the loading on Thursday. ... ... ... One more time. We need a dedicated team for the loading on Thursday.

The word is, receipt. In this sentence, it means, the act of receiving something. For example, please confirm receipt of the passport copy. Now say it with me. Please confirm receipt of the flight details. ... ... ... One more time. Please confirm receipt of the flight details.

The word is, revised. It means, changed and corrected. For example, the supplier will send a revised quotation after the next loading. Now say it with me. Please send me the revised quotation for the racks today. ... ... ... One more time. Please send me the revised quotation for the racks today.

The expression is, rather than. It means, instead of. For example, rather than forwarding the email to others, please check it yourself and reply here. Now say it with me. Rather than waiting until Friday, please send what you have now. ... ... ... One more time. Rather than waiting until Friday, please send what you have now.
Now three words from last Saturday's test. You missed these, so listen carefully.

The word is, outstanding. In work English, it means, not done yet, still waiting. It does not mean excellent here. For example, the photos and the quotation are still outstanding. Now say it with me. The thread table is still outstanding. ... ... ... One more time. The thread table is still outstanding.

The word is, feasible. It means, possible to do in real life. For example, please let me know if this sheet is feasible on the floor. Now say it with me. Is it feasible to finish racks seven and eight by Thursday? ... ... ... One more time. Is it feasible to finish racks seven and eight by Thursday?

The expression is, comply with. It means, to follow a rule or a standard. Remember, we say comply with, not comply to. For example, the supplier complies with the buyer's chemical list. Now say it with me. We must comply with the customs rules before the count. ... ... ... One more time. We must comply with the customs rules before the count.
Part seven. Role-play.
It is eight forty-five in the morning. Anthony goes to Trinh Do's desk in the EXIM office. Listen first.
Anthony: Good morning, Trinh. Do you have a minute?
Trinh: Good morning, Mr Lee. Yes, of course.
Anthony: Thank you for your replies yesterday. Two items are still outstanding. The thread table and the September ledger.
Trinh: Sorry, Mr Lee. Yesterday we were busy with the GOH frames for the Vince shipment.
Anthony: I understand. But the physical count is on Saturday. I need the thread numbers before I report to Mr Moon.
Trinh: How many shipments do you need? All of them?
Anthony: Yes, every shipment from COATS PHONG PHU without a declaration. Please show the invoice number, the date received, the quantity, and the current stock.
Trinh: I think I can finish the table by eleven. The ledger may take longer.
Anthony: That's fine. Please send the table by eleven a.m. For the ledger, can you send it by five p.m.?
Trinh: Yes, I will ask Hien to help me.
Anthony: Good idea. Share the work with your team. If something is not feasible, please tell me early.
Trinh: OK, Mr Lee. I will update you as soon as the table is ready.
Anthony: Thank you, Trinh.
Later, Anthony meets Mr Moon in his office. Listen once more.
Anthony: Mr Moon, I have an update on the thread without customs declaration. Trinh will send the full table by eleven a.m.
Mr Moon: Good. How many shipments are affected?
Anthony: I will know the exact number at eleven. Then I will bring you two options before lunch.
Mr Moon: OK. Please make sure we comply with the customs rules before Saturday.
Anthony: Yes, sir. I will update you as soon as I have the numbers.
Now let's practice two key sentences.
Sentence one. Two items are still outstanding. ... ... ... One more time. Two items are still outstanding.
Sentence two. If something is not feasible, please tell me early. ... ... ... One more time. If something is not feasible, please tell me early.
Part eight. Closing.
Here is the one thing to do today. Get the thread table from Trinh by eleven a.m., and report the plan to Mr Moon before lunch.
After that, check Mr Asanka's flight choice, and send Mai one short reminder. The rest can follow.
You are ready. Speak slowly and clearly today. Have a good Wednesday, Anthony. See you tomorrow morning.
